name: LLM-Pruner: On the Structural Pruning of Large Language Models
problem: Compressing an LLM usually means task-specific pruning, which destroys general capability, and recovery normally needs the original (enormous) training corpus.
mechanism: TASK-AGNOSTIC STRUCTURAL pruning under two constraints (stay general, need little of the original data): use gradient information from a small calibration set to identify non-critical COUPLED structures - groups of parameters that must be removed together - rather than independent weights, so the remaining model stays a valid architecture. Recovery is done with LoRA, not full fine-tuning, which is what makes the 50K-example budget sufficient.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claim (abstract): performance of the pruned models recovered via LoRA 'in merely 3 HOURS, requiring only 50K data', validating on LLaMA, Vicuna and ChatGLM with the compressed models retaining 'satisfactory' zero-shot classification and generation. COMPRESSION RATIO: structured pruning (whole groups/structures removed), so the ratio depends on the pruning budget chosen - no single ratio is quoted in the abstract. QUALITY COST: the meaningful cost is not perplexity but the LoRA recovery budget (3 h / 50K examples), which is the number to compare against.
